To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

chronic exercise has different effect on adiponectin than does weight-matched food-restriction in hyperphagic OLETF rats, and the elevated plasma testosterone in exercising rats might be a reason for the difference in adiponectin regulation.
12-week chronic exercise induces different effects of plasma adiponectine than does food restriction in OLETF rats.
12-week wheel exercise induced different effects on plasma level of adiponectine than did food restriction, despite the similar reduction in bodyweight, fat volume and plasma levels of leptin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between voluntary wheel running exercise and plasma adiponectine level in hyperphagic, hyperleptinemic, obese OLETF rat.
the effects of chronic voluntary exercise on adiponectin levels in hyperphagic, obese OLETF model rats.
the effects of exercise on adiponectin, which may provide insight into the mechanisms by which exercise improves metabolic health.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
chronic exercise does not increase plasma adiponectine level in hyperphagic obese OLETF rat.
the effect of chronic voluntary wheel running exercise on plasma adiponctin level is different from that of body weight reduction.
voluntary wheel running exercise does not increase blood adiponectine level, despite a similar reduction in body fat mass and plasma leptine concentration, compared with food restriction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
voluntary wheel running exercise is not a good strategy for increasing circulating adiponectin levels.
chronic voluntary exercise may have a negative effect on plasma adiponecitn concentration in hyperphagic OLETF rats.
voluntary wheel running exercise is not an effective method to induce hyperadiponetinemia in hyperphagic OLETF rats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
adiponectin is not regulated by exercise in the same manner as it is by food restriction.
the effects of exercise on plasma adiponctein level may not be solely due to body weight reduction.
adiponectin is not a simple marker for adiposity and that the adiposity-independent effects of exercise should be considered when interpreting adiponectin levels in humans and other animals.
